description: In the cover letter editor's Signature tab, the name field asks for first and last name, and the two address fields show a neutral example in the letter's language.

userStories.title: The name field asks for first and last name
userStories.description: As a job seeker filling in my signature, I want the name field to say it expects my first and last name, so that the letter is signed with my full name.
acceptanceCriteria: The Signature tab's name field label reads exactly: "Votre prénom et nom" under `/fr`; "Your first and last name" under `/en`; "Ihr Vorname und Name" under `/de`; "Il tuo nome e cognome" under `/it`.
The label follows the interface language, like the other labels of the tab.
The name field's placeholder, value, saving and printing are unchanged.

FR-1: The two address examples come from the same per-language letter wording the editor already resolves (`COVER_LETTER_WORDING` for `coverLetterLanguage(...)`). The language is not resolved a second time.
FR-2: The name label stays an interface-dictionary string with parity across fr/en/de/it (`coverLetters.editor.signature.nameLabel`).

FR-3: The interface dictionary keys that are no longer read (`streetPlaceholder` and `postalLocalityPlaceholder`) are removed from all four locales, and nothing reads them. The same was done for `greetingPlaceholder` in cover-letter-swiss-format US-005.
FR-4: No new dependency, column, route or migration.
Regression constraint: The other Signature tab labels and placeholders still follow the interface language and keep their current text.
Regression constraint: The preview, the PDF and the Word export of an unchanged letter print the same text as before.
Regression constraint: Saving the sender fields still stores what the user typed. An emptied field still stores `''`, and a never-set field is still `null`, which falls back to the linked CV.
Regression constraint: The Recipient tab is unchanged.
Regression constraint: The e-mail validation and length limits of the sender fields are unchanged.
Verification: The mandatory baseline from `CLAUDE.md` §14: typecheck, test, test:integration, test:e2e, build, and lint at or below the tracked ceiling (286).

Verification: `pnpm test:visual` and `pnpm test:parity` must stay at their current results (visual 10/10; parity MATCH 211 / KNOWN 3 / NEW 0). A changed baseline is a FAIL unless the only difference is the text this PRD changes.

Verification: e2e: under each of `/fr`, `/en`, `/de` and `/it`, the name label text; a German letter under `/fr` and a French letter under `/de`: the two exact placeholders with empty fields and no linked CV address; an existing spec that asserts the old label or placeholders is updated only as far as this change requires.
Verification: Unit: the per-language address examples, for the four languages.
Verification: Browser: rendered evidence of the Signature tab in fr and de, at 1280 and 375, showing the label in full (not clipped) and both placeholders.
Verification: `ui-expert` PASS and `code-reviewer` PASS.
FAIL condition: Wrong text: any label or placeholder differs from the exact text above.
FAIL condition: Wrong language: a placeholder follows the interface language instead of the letter's language.
FAIL condition: Prefix: a placeholder keeps an "ex. :" / "e.g.," / "z.B." / "es." prefix.
FAIL condition: Leak into output: a placeholder is stored, or printed in the preview, PDF or Word.
FAIL condition: Clipping: the new label is clipped at 375 or 1280.
FAIL condition: Scope: another field, label or tab changes text.
FAIL condition: Second resolver: the letter language is resolved by a second, separate rule.
BLOCKER condition: The letter's language cannot be read in the Signature tab without resolving it a second way.
BLOCKER condition: A required check cannot run.
Out of scope: Other fields: the name field's placeholder, the phone, e-mail and annexes fields, and the Recipient tab's fields and labels.
Out of scope: Output: what is stored or printed. The preview, PDF and Word output are unchanged.
Out of scope: Other wording: the other labels, which keep following the interface language.
Out of scope: Language detection: how the letter's language is detected.
Out of scope: Pre-existing decisions carried over from cover-letter-swiss-format: the ß in the sign-off options, the Generate fallback, and placeholder contrast.

userStories.title: The address fields show a neutral example in the letter's language
userStories.description: As a job seeker, I want the street and postcode fields to show a neutral example in my letter's language, so that I know what to type without the example naming a real place in another language.
acceptanceCriteria: When empty, the "Rue et numéro" field shows exactly this placeholder, according to the letter's language: fr "Rue du Bourg 12"; de "Dorfstrasse 12"; it "Via del Borgo 12"; en "12 Main Street".
When empty, the "NPA et localité" field shows exactly this placeholder, according to the letter's language: fr "1234 Ma ville"; de "1234 Mein Ort"; it "1234 La mia città"; en "1234 My town".
Neither placeholder has an "ex. :", "e.g.,", "z.B." or "es." prefix.

The letter's language is the one the preview prints in. Two cases must hold: a German letter opened under `/fr` shows "Dorfstrasse 12" and "1234 Mein Ort"; a French letter opened under `/de` shows "Rue du Bourg 12" and "1234 Ma ville".
If the user edits the letter's text so that its detected language changes, the two placeholders follow, as the greeting placeholder does.
Labels, values, saving, the CV fallback and the printed letter are unchanged. A placeholder is never stored or printed.

FR-1: The two address examples come from the same per-language letter wording the editor already resolves (`COVER_LETTER_WORDING` for `coverLetterLanguage(...)`). The language is not resolved a second time.
